div.head: ASSOCIATION.
div.p: ASSOCIATION.

I have a word of praise for W.A.C. this week. They beat St. Helens Junction by a goal to nil on Saturday. The St. Helens team is a good one and has beaten the St. Elphins twice. This ought to be material for local prophets, as the W.A.C. and St. Elphins are to meet on Saturday next. In addition to this victory, I want also to mention that the W.A.C. turned out a good re- serve team against the Grammar School. This is a healthy sign which I am glad to see.

It has been whispered that there is a likelihood of Everton sending, a team down to Warrington to play a town team consisting of representatives of all the local clubs. I sincerely hope that this "comes off have a beneficial I hope enciale Ever ton the Association game in Warring- tnton will look at it in that light and do a good deed for the game of which they are such redoubt- able exponents.

The Widnes Parish Church team applied for admission into the association medal competition, but were rightly excluded. A sub-committee has been formed to arrange the opening of the competition and the following draws have been made :-Ist round to be played on or before March 25th, Warrington Cricket v. Padg,,ate Institute. The following have byes : Warrington, Lymm, St. Elphins, Warrington North End, Penketh, Orford Crescent, Orford Barracks. 2nd round to be played on or before April 3rd :—Warrington North End v. Lymm ; Padgate Institute V. St. Elphins ; Penketh v. Warrington ; Orford Crescent v. Orford Barracks. The first-named clubs have choice of grounds.

div.head: WIDNES TOWN COUNCIL.
div.p: WIDNES TOWN COUNCIL.

The second quarterly meeting of this Council was held at the Town Hall on Tuesday. The Mayor (Alderman Gossage) presided, and there were present Aldermen Sadler, Tiromts, Williamson Councillors Owen, Davies, Hodgkinson, Quinn, H. Singleton, Fitzpatrick, W. W. Gossage, T. Smith, P. Longton, T. Shuttleworth, W. Christie, F. Neil,
Balrougl;_, C. E. Barlow, Carney, G. I. Neil, H. S.
Oppenirieim (town clerk), T. Craik (deputy cleric) S. Hoyle (accountant), 1. Carr (engineer), J. S. Sin- clair (surveyor), Dr. O'Keeffe (medical officer), and W. Lowe (nuisance inspector.)
RAILWAY RATES AND CRARGES. A communication was read from the Town Clerk of

Carlisle, asking the Council to adopt resolutions protest- ing against the new classification and new rates and charges, on the respective railwa?s.—The Mayor said lie did not exactly know in what way the Council could interfere in this matter, and he suggested that the com- munication be passed on to the _General Purposes Corn-
mittee. Alderman Timmis moved and Councillor F. Neil
seconded a resolution to that effect. Carried.

AN IMPERIAL PENNY POST. A letter was read from the Secretary to the south of Scotland Chamber of Commerce, writing the Council to adopt a memorial in favour of an Imperial Penny Post. —This letter was referred to the General Purposes Com- mittee, on the motion of Alderman Thnmis,seconded by Councillor F. Nei/.
The Highway .Committee reported that .the Borough

Surveyor submitted plan and estimate for the Bewaring and improvement of Peelhouse-lane from a point near to No. 2 Peelhouse-lane to Millfield-road, and it was re- solved that the work of sewering be proceeded with at an estimated cost 011210, and that the Surveyor be in- structed to ascertain; the terms upon which land caa be acquired for the improvement of the lane as shown upon the plan. The Surveyor submitted plans and estimates for the sewering of Appleton district,and it was resolved that the same be approved, and that the Town Clerk be instructed to make-application to the Local Government _.

Board for the borrowing of £520, the amount estimated to be required to carry out the work. At the latter meeting the Surveyor reported that "In accordance with the Committe's instructions lam proceeding wit the extension of the sewer in this lane. The work _ _ _ _ _
commenced on the 16th ult., pipes have been laid as far as Taylor-st. The average No. of men employed per day is 30. lam in communication with the owners ad- .. _
r7' joining respecting the purchase of land required for the

widening." Letter, eth January ult., from Mr. J. Ison, postmaster, asking for permission for the erection of a pillar letter box at the corner of Bank-street, Mersey- road, read. Resolved—that the application be granted, and that the Town Clerk reply to the letter suggesting that better postal facilities should also be afforded in the neighbourhood of Ann-street west for the Newtown dis- trict, and at Hanging Birches for the Farnworth district. Resolved upon the application of the United Alkali Co., Ltd.,that,subject to the terms of an agreement to be ore- ' pared by the Town Clerk, the Corporation raise no objection to the Co. constructing a level railway crossing in Tan- house-lane at the point mentioned in the Alkali Co.'s letter. The Surveyor submitted plan prepared by Mr.C.L.Evans, surveyor to Sir Richard Brooke, showing a proposed alteration in the line of roadway in Gorsey-lane,to which the approval of the Corporation was asked. Resolved that the proposal be not entertained but that the Sur- veyor intorm Mr. Evans that the Committee will be pre- pared to consider an amended scheme based upon a give and take line in equal proportions. Alderman Sadler in moving the adoption of the minu- tes, said they had commenced the work of newering Appleton district and Peelhouse-lane earlier than they should have done in order to provide employment for the unemployed, and on that account they had presumed that the Council would forgive the Commissioners for trespassing on their prerogative.—Councillor Shuttle- worth seconded.—ln reply to Councillor Bullough,Aider- man Sadler said the present seheine for sewering Apple- ton would complete the drainage of that locality. (Hear, hear.)—The minutes were adopted. THE HEALTH or TILE TOWN.—INSANITA Ea PROPERTY. . _

The following reports were made to the Health Com- mittee : Accident Hospital—Number of patients at last meeting, 19 ; admitted since, 7; discharged, 8 ; died, 2 ; patients still in, 7. Infectious Diseases Hospital—Num- ber of patients at last meeting, 5: ; admitted since, 2 ; discharged since, 4 ; patients still in 3. It was resolved thrt a sewing machine be purchased for the Infectious Diseases Hospital. The Medical Officer of Health reported that during the past month these were 107 births and 78 deaths being, at the respective rates of 34.24 and 24.96 per 1,000. The deaths included 24 chil- dren under one year, and 16 between one and five ye trs. Zytnotic diseases caused 11 deaths and there was one inquest. Notifications of Infectious Diseases as folhws were received : Enteric or typhoid Fever, 3; erysipelas, 4 ; diphtheria, 3 ; membranous croup, 3 ; puerperal fever, 1 ; scarlet fever, 5•; smallpox, 1 ; total, 20. The Medical Officer added " In consequence of the alteration of the day of the Health Committee meeting the mortal- ity returns appear higher than they would be otherwise, as they include the last week in December as well as the four weeks of .nuary. Besides the death rate from diseases of the respiratory organs has been unusually high this month. One case of smallpox has been noti- fied on the 23rd January, and prompt measures were taken for its isolation. Since then no case has occurred. There is ample accommodation at the new smallpox hospital, which is now fit for the reception of patients, should any other cases of that disease occur in this borough. Two houses, 89 and 71, Lugsdale-road, which were occupied as dwellings, have received my attention, and I signed certificates condemn- ing them as unfit for human habitation. The Town Clerk reported the service of notice upon Mr. Thomas Kershaw, the owner of houses No. 69 and 71, Luasdale-road,.reqniring him to show cause why an 'order should not be made for the closing of this property. Mr. Kershaw attended the meeting. Resolved—That the owner having failed to show sufficiest cause why such buildings should not be declared unfit for human habitation the Corporation do, by writings under their seal, declare that such. buildings. are respectively unfit for human habitation, and direct that unless and until such buildings shall have been rendered fit for human habitation, they be closed and the use thereof for human habitation prohibited, and that for this purpose the seal of the Corporation be affixed to the form of order prescribed by the bye-laws now in force. TIM SMALLPDX. ROSPITAL.

Councillor G. I. Neil in moving the adoption of the minutes of the Health Committee, said the smallpox hospital was now in an efficient and complete state. It was substantially built and equal to a brick building,and Will fitted up with all modernappliances. He had on behalf of the Committee to thank the Mayor for his kindness in giving them the benefit of hiaadvice in the erection of the building and also for supplying them with silicate paint, with which the hospital was covered, making it impervious to water and fire-proof. There had bean two cases of smallpox, One notified on the 23rd January, and the other on the 10th February and he was sorry to say that there had been a false ending to the latter case.—Mr. Smith seconded the motion.—Carried. 41LS AND WATER COMMITTEE. The Engineer (Mr. Can), submitted to the Gas and Water Committee correspondence with Mr. Morrison iv a proposed increased water consumption at Mathie- son's Works and stated :—As the existing 91n main is of insufficient capacity for the proposed demand. I would recommend that an additional 9in. main be laid into this district from Ditton-road by way of Marsh-road. The length would be 436; yards, and the estimated cost £250. Resolved that an additional gin. main be laid from Dit- ton road by way of Marsh-road to Mathieson's Works,at an estimate cost of £2so.—Proposed new gas holder at Dime :—The original design was for a tank 1081 t. 6in. in diameter and 25f1. deep, to accommodate a triple lift holder having a capacity of 605,000, cubic feet. It will be seen that a tank of this dia:neter, would occupy the whole of the available space at the proposed site within the Corporation boundary. During the past month, however, a number of trial bare holes have been sunk which show that the quick-sand frequently met with in this district immediately underlying the up- land clay is so near the surface as to render the making of a tank 25ft. deep, impracticable. It would he running a dangerous risk both as to the stability and tightness of the tank to cut through the clay into the quick-sand at any one point. The strata indicated by the borings will admit of a tank 23 feet deep being made, but with 21t. less in depth and the same diameter the capacity of the holder would he reduced from the proposed 605,000 cubic feet to 554,000 cubit feet. Under these circumstances a second tank 118 feet diameter and 23 feet deep has been designed, the gas holder capacity of which would be 605,000 cubic feet. To give room for this tank, however, it wit be necessary to obtain a strip of land 12 feet wide and 476-ft. 6-in, long, or 635 super. yards in all, now occu- piedby the Liver Works of the United Alkali Company. I have ascertained from the Company through Mr. Morrison, that arrangements could most likely be made for the Corporation to acquire the land in the event of their deciding to erect the larger gasholder. The esti- mated cost of the tank and holder is £7,ooo.—Alderman Timmis moved, and Councillor Davies seconded the adoption of the minutes. AUTOMATIC METRES. Alderman Sadler said he had on previous occasions drawn the attention of the Health Committee to auto- matic gas meters by which consumers could obtain gas when required h; placing a penny in the meter. There were now 7,000 at work in Liverpool, and it was com- puted that there would be 13,000 in use in a few months,ancl as the meter had proved so beneficial in Liver- pool he saw no reason why it should not in Widnes,and he wished to know if the Committee would deal with the question.—Alderman Timmis said he did not know any- thing about the subject and he did not suppose the Com- mittee qid, and the question had not been brought before the Committee before. The Committee however, would give the subject consideration.—The minutes were passed.

div.head: TECHNICAL INSTRUCTION COMMITTER.
div.p: TECHNICAL INSTRUCTION COMMITTER.

To this Committee the Secretary submitted detailed estimate of articles likely to be required in connection with the proposed new Technical Schools, amounting to £650. and tke same was approved, and the Town Clerk was instructed to make application to the County Coun- cil for a grant in aid of the articles named. Resolved— that subject to the approval of the Science and Art Department, Mr. S. Hoyle be appointed Special Local Secretary and Custodian of examination papers for the forthcoming examinations. Accounts amounting to £8 Is. ad., examined and passed for payment. The minutes were approved on the proposition of Councillor P. Neil.

div.head: PEOPIMFD CEMETERY.
div.p: PEOPIMFD CEMETERY.

_ Councillor Hodgkinson moved that the Town Clerk be instructed to obtain returns of the numbers of inter- ments which have taken place at each of the various burial places in Widnes during the last three years, and of the unoccupied space at each of such burial places, and to forward particulars of the same to each member of the Council prior to the next Council meeting. He ' said he was satisfied that the existing burial accommo- dation was inadequate, and be wished the information as a first step towards moving in the matter of a ceme- tery.—Alderman Timmis seconded the motion.—Coun- cillor G. I. Neil said the Council had many expensive schemes on at the present time, and he said the raising of the question of a cemetery was premature.—The Mayor said the Council ought to have the benefit of the information, but they would not need to take action un- til there had arisen actual necessity.—The motion was carried.

div.head: COMMOTION OF THE TOWN HALL.
div.p: THE COMMOTION OF THE TOWN HALL.

In the absence of Alderman Wareing, who had given notice of the motion, Alderman Timmis moved "That the General Purposes and Parliamentary Committee be instructed to inquire and report to the Council as to what additions or alterations are required to the Town Hall Buildings for the purposes of the Corporation ; and as to the desirability of providing in connection there- with suitable assembly rooms and other accommodation for the public. And•that the Cemmitte be authorised to obtain plans and estimates, and for such purpose to em- ploy an architect or architects."—Councillor Singleton seconded.—Councillor F. Neil agreed with the resolution to a large extent, but he moved' an amendment that the last sentence be omitted.—Councillor Shuttlevrorth seconded.—The Myor did not see how they could got a proper report without employing an archi- tect.—Alderman Timmis said no definite action would be taken without the consent of the Council. The in- tention now was to obtain information.—Mr. Neil, after this explanation, withdrew his amendment. The Mayor said it must be admitted by the whole Council that they had absolutely no accommodation at present for the services of the town.--Councillor Quinn proposed that the Committee prepare a report with the assistance) of the surveyor.—Councillor Smith said he entirely objected to the completion of the Town Hall at the pre- sent time. It would mean a great outlay of money.— Alderman Sadler seconded the amendment, for which 5 voted and 14- against.—Councillor Smith then moved that the subject be put back until that day twelve months.—Councillbr Longton seconded.—This amend- ment was also lost, only three voting for it.—Councillor Davies proposed that the discussion be adjourned for a month .—Councillor Christie seconded the amendment, which was lost, only three voting for it. The original motion was then carried by eleven votes to eight.

div.head: FRODSHAM.
div.p: FRODSHAM.

DISTRESSINCI, Stricins.—On Tuesday afternoon an in- quiry into the circumstances connected with the death of Thomas Thorne Rodger, aged 48 years, tailor of Main- -81., Frodsham, was held by Mr. H. Churten, at the Red Lion Hotel. Mr. Edmundson, was the foreman of the jury.—Martha Rodger, wife of the deceased, stated that her husband had been very depressed in spirits for some time on account of losing his sight, fie lost one eye 22 years agO, and since then the ether had grown weaker and weaker, until he was almost,if not altogether blind. On Monday morning she saw him in his bedroom, and on going upstairs a quarter of an hour later, she found him suspended by the neck to the bedpost with a piece' of thick string. She screamed and called in Mrs. Clays from neat door, who immediately came.—Mrs. Clays de. posed that she had noticed of late that Mr. Rodger was in very low spirits. She never suspected that he woald take away his own life. On hearing screams by the previous witness she ran in, and saw him hanging. She secured a knife, and cut down the body. Life was ex- tinct.—The Coroner said the case was a very distressing one.--The jury retured a verdict that the deceased com- mitted, suicide whilst in a state of temporary in- sanitary, brought on by the loss of his sight. THE RAILWAY STATION.—The newly-erected office adjoining the warehouse in the Railway Company's new goods yard was opened for business on Monday morn- ing. The sidings on the southerly side of the station will., no doubt, prove much more convenient and advan- tageous to those engaged in the coal business, both buyers, and sellers, and also for the loading and un- loading of farmers' produce, than was the old yard. CHURCH OF ENGLAND BAND OF HOPE.—A kinder- spiel, entitled "Day of Rest and Gladness," was given in the National Girls' school, on Monday evening, to a thronged audience. The characters were represented by nine girls and five boys, members of the Band of Hope, the chorus comprising about sixty voices, accom- panied by Miss Thomas' string band. Although at times there was some degree of hesitation, the whole of the sacred play was performed in a very striking man- ner by the children.

FOUND DROWNED IN WESTON CANAL.-011 Thursday morning, shortly before seven o'clock, William Savage, lock tenter, employed on the Weaver Navigation. at Weston Point, recovered the body of a dead man the canal at that . place. The body was subsequently identified as that of John Houston, a blacksmith, aged 48, and residing at Frodsham Marsh. He was last seen alive by a fellow lodger named William Bellis, a black- smith, about a month ago. The deceased, he says, then set out for Runcorn.

WESLEYAN HOME MISSIONS.—Sermons were preached in the Trinity Chapel, Frodsham, on Sunday, by the Rev. J. Hanby, of Halton, and on Tuesday a public meeting was held, which was presided over by Mr. R. Posnett, of Runcorn. Sister Annetta, from the Salford Mission gave a very interesting description of the work of the mission. There was a large convregatitaa present, and the affertories amounted to over £7.

div.head: PRESBYTERIAN ANNUAL TEA PARTY. -- ALDERMAN FRANCOMB ON BRITISH EDUCATION AND FOREIGN COMPETITION.
div.p: PRESBYTERIAN ANNUAL TEA PARTY. -- ALDERMAN FRANCOMB ON BRITISH EDUCA- TION AND FOREIGN COMPETITION.

The annual tea party and entertainment in con- nection with the St. John's Presbyterian Church, were held in the school adjoining that church on Thursday evening. About 80 persona partook of tea, and at the subsequent entertainment Alderman Francomb (the deputy Mayor) presided. A pro- gramme of songs, recitations, pianoforte and violoncello 50105,,&c., was gone through, the following taking part: —Messrs. Dunsmuir, Bamford, Blackburn, Furness, Armstrong, and Longdin, Miss Armstrong, and Masters E. Jtmes and J. Owen. The Chairman delivered an address in the course of the evening. He said that one thing he noticed about St. John's, congregation, that they never figured in the newspapers as quarrelling one with another, and in this they differed from many other congregations. fie thought there was nothing so bad as tosee religious people fall out and figure in the papers. He referred to Sunday schools, and said there was an immense amount of money spent every year by the Government of the country in providing a good secular education for the young, and within the last few years arrangements had been made whereby almost every boy and girl who wished it could have a very advanced technical education. In Warrington they had good technical classes, which were carried on with much success. He could not too strongly recommend boys and girls te attend these classes. It had been demon- strated over and over again that unless Englishmen could keep pace with the times they would be run off the markets of the earth. There was a time when an Englishman could do what foreigners could not do. We were then far in advance of them in the manufacture of almost everything, but at the present moment the foreigner was running us pretty closely. If we wanted te hold our own as a prosperous nation we must pay serious attention to education. They might fill a boy full of arithmetic, French, grammar, &c., but they must not neglect to give him a religious education. There did not seem to be time to do this in the day „ schools,and therefere it was the bounden duty of Sunday I school teachers,parents,and clergymen to see that children ' were well grounded in the elements of sound religious education. He thought this could not be better im- parted than in the Sunday school. It was astonishing the amount of influence a Sunday school teacher had over children, and early impressions were scarcely ever forgotten.—The Rev. J. WARNOCK also made some remarks, and said that during the past year, though trade had been bad and the town in an unsatisfactory condition as to health, there had been an increase of membership, and the ordinary revenue of the church had not been affected, while no members ha bean lost by death.

RUNCORN WATER BILL. pURSUAJIT to a requisition in writing of 25 owners of property and ratepayers in the Distriot of the Runcorn Improvement Commissioners, I do HEREBY GIVE NOTICE that a PUBLIC MEETING of the owners and ratepayers of the Di trict of the Runcorn Improvement Commissioners will be held, pursuant to the provisions of an Act of the 35th and 36th Victoria cap. 91, entitulecl "An Act " to Authorise the application of funds of Municipal Corpora- tions and other governing bodies in certain cases "at BETHESDA LECTURE HALL, VICAR-STREET, RUNCORN On THURSDAY the 16T0 day of FEBRUARY, 1893, At seven o'clock in the evening. For the purpose of considering certain resolutions passed by the said Improvement Con-missioners on the 28th day of November. 1892, and if thought desirable, of passing a resolu- tion confirming the said resolutions of the said Improvement Commissioners, and authorising them to take such steS as they shall deem necessary for promoting a Bill in the ensu- ing Session of Parliament intituled " A Bill to authorise the Runcorn Improvement Commissioners to acquire the under- taking of the Runcorn, Weston, and Halton Waterworks Company, and to confer further powers on the Commis- sioners.' Dated this 8 h day of February, 1893. Town Hall, Runcorn. FRANCIS IVISWALL, Chairman. Runcorn Improvement Commissioners.

Passage between Rolleston Street, and Allen Street. „ Noi. 46 to 80 Allen Street, and Nos. 38 to 66 Bewsey Street. „ behind Nos. 16 to 34 Allen Street, and between Nos. 12 and 16 Allen Street. NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN, that the Town Council of the Borough of Warrington, acting as the Urban Authority, have resolved that each of the above streets shall be levelled, paved, metalled, flagged, channelled, and made good, in pursuance of Section 6of the above Act, and have further resolved that the specification, plan and section, estimate, and provisional apportionment, prepared by the Borough Surveyor, in repect of each such street, be approved. The said specifications, plans and sections estimates, and provisional apportionments, or duly certified copies thereof, will be deposited during one month from the 11th day of February, 1893, at the offices of the Borough Surveyor at the Town Hall, and will be open to inspection at all reasonable times. BRUNNER, MON D, AND CO., LIMITED. • A PROSPEROUS CONCERN. The directors of this firm of alkali manufacturers, whose works are at , Winnington, Northwich, have just published their half-yearly report, which shows a balance to the credit of profit and loss account on the working for the half-year ended 31st December last of £287,092 18s. 2d., which, with the amount of £78,518 2s. Bd. brought forward from the previous half - year, makes a total of £343,810 18s. 10d. It is proposed to deal with the balance as follows :—Dividend on the preference capital at 7 per cent., per annum, £15,358 ss. dividend on the ordinary capital at 50 per cent, Per annum, £152,500; amount to be written off patents account, £2,b00; balance to be carried forward, £173,254 13s. 10d. The reserve fund is so large that the directors do not at present propose to increase At the forthcoming annual meeting of shareholders a resolution will be submitted that the nominal capital of the company shall be increase 1 to £2,000,000 by the creation of new shares.

THE SUGGESTED MINERS' HOLIDAY. On 'Monday the Council of the Yorkshire Mined Association held a largely attended meeting at liarnslel• when the recommendation of the Executive Committee of the Miners' Federation for a general holiday was dis- cussed. Mr. Cowey, president of the Association, and Mr. Parrott, both of whom belong to the Federation Executive, were present. A resolution was carried agreeing with the suggestion of the Executive that a Conference be called in Birmingham on the 28th inst. in order to get all the mining distracts to agree to a stop Page of work. It was resolved that a ballot should be takeo at every branch in order to ascertain the feelings of Oa men on the question. THE SHIP CANAL. OLDHAM AND THE CANAL.
